newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber ends down on buyers' reserve.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber ends down on buyers' reserve.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices fell at the close after another day of fruitless trading, dealers said.

Buyers were seeking cheaper prices, similar to those they could obtain in Indonesia, while producers were reluctant to comply because of higher costs and tighter supply of raw materials due to the wintering period, dealers said.
"We can't afford to go as low as the Indonesian prices everyday," said a trader. "If we follow them, we'll have to eat wind, as the Chinese say."

At the close, the benchmark April RSS1 buyer was quoted at 304.50 cents ($) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB), down one cent from Monday's close. The board quoted April SMR20 buyer 1.50 cents lower at 291.
Traders offered the SMR20 at 292 cents a kg, SMR CV at 357, SMR L at 337, SMR 5 at 209, SMR 10 at 294 and latex at 234.
The strengthening of the ringgit against the dollar could also be a reason for the weak demand, said traders.
The INRO five-day average was unchanged at 232.18 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on March 17 from 232.39 Mar 14. The daily indicator was at 232.04 from 231.97 previously.
